canonical_topic: Locational basis in natural gas markets
definition: In natural gas (and energy markets generally), basis refers to the price difference between two physical trading locations, most commonly the difference between a specific delivery point and the Henry Hub, the sole liquid NYMEX settlement location.
core_idea: Because futures only deliver to one physical point, traders use the term basis to describe how much a given location's price differs from the futures delivery price, and basis swaps let them convert a Henry Hub-referenced position into exposure at a different physical location.
key_points: Henry Hub is described as the only liquid natural gas trading location and is the NYMEX futures settlement point.
Basis swaps let users combine NYMEX futures with a swap that exchanges the Henry Hub price for the price at a different physical location.
Because futures have only a single delivery point, "basis" in energy/gas trading most commonly means the price gap between a specific location and that futures delivery point.
relationships: Directly follows from the general point that energy-market basis is locational rather than time-based.
Basis swaps connect futures exposure (single delivery point) to a trader's actual physical location need.
trading_implications: A trader needing gas at a location other than Henry Hub can combine NYMEX futures with a basis swap to get location-specific price exposure.
